title: Characterizing Recoverable Expert-Utilization Signatures in Fine-Tuned Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2610.41039v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: As Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language models are increasingly deployed in distributed environments, from federated learning to edge-cloud systems, their architecture harbors an underexplored landscape of security vulnerabilities. Moving beyond textual analysis, we uncover structural memorization: a novel vulnerability where a fine-tuned model memorizes not only its training data but also the internal pathway used to process it, creating a characteristic routing fingerprint unique to the training process. We provide comprehensive empirical evidence that structural memorization emerges consistently even from a few samples, and that its intensity is directly influenced by the choice of trainable modules.   We show that these memorized expert pathways can be stealthily recovered through the model's unconditional generation, using only routing and output logits, with no knowledge of the fine-tuning data or procedure. translated_title: 刻画微调混合专家大语言模型中可恢复的专家使用签名
translated_abstract: 随着混合专家大语言模型越来越多地被部署在分布式环境中——从联邦学习到边云系统——其架构中潜藏着一个尚未被充分探索的安全漏洞领域。超越文本分析的范畴，我们揭示了“结构化记忆”这一新型漏洞：微调后的模型不仅会记住其训练数据，还会记住用于处理这些数据的内部路径，从而形成训练过程所特有的路由指纹。我们提供了全面的实证证据，表明即使仅从少量样本出发，结构化记忆也会持续出现，且其强度直接受可训练模块选择的影响。我们证明，这些被记忆的专家路径可以通过模型的无条件生成被隐秘地恢复，攻击者仅需路由信息和输出logits，无需了解微调数据或微调过程。在分布式部署场景中……
tldr: 该论文揭示了微调混合专家大语言模型中一种名为“结构化记忆”的新型安全漏洞：模型会将训练数据的内部专家路由路径记忆为独特指纹，攻击者无需了解微调数据或过程，仅凭模型无条件生成时的路由信息和输出logits即可隐秘恢复这些路径。
en_tdlr: This paper uncovers a novel vulnerability in fine-tuned Mixture-of-Experts LLMs termed "structural memorization," where models memorize the internal expert-routing pathways of their training data as unique fingerprints, which adversaries can stealthily recover through unconditional generation using only routing and output logits—without any knowledge of the fine-tuning data or procedure.
